record.tranche_reason: Tests representation of synthetic multi-dimensional features and known GPT-2 circular subspaces using SAE measurements, rather than reproducing the original superposition method.
record.gate_note: The post reports results on circle recovery, feature splitting, SAE metrics, and learned groups. Results about proposed approaches that were not tried, and the author's uncertainty about how to measure success, are not rows. Learned-group-space embedding results are not rows because they do not measure the claim versions' representational properties.
record.test_reason: The post builds and evaluates Group SAE variants for finding multi-dimensional features. It uses known circular features (the authors' earlier paper) and a hand-built synthetic circle dataset as ground truth, and reports mainly how well its own method performs. It does not test whether networks store features in superposition (V1), whether polysemanticity comes from capacity (V2/V3), or whether features are one-dimensional (V6). The synthetic circles are constructed by the authors, not learned by a network. The GPT-2 month circle is a sanity re-check of the prior paper's result, made to evaluate the SAEs.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The author says the Group SAE results were not compelling and did not accomplish anything useful. He doubts dictionary learning is the right tool for multi-dimensional features. He also notes it is unclear how to measure success, or whether the groups found are truly multi-dimensional rather than correlated 1-D features.
record.recipe_differences: The post experiments with group-sparsity SAE variants and learned groups to find multidimensional features; it does not reproduce the original Toy Models of Superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Group size and penalty choices affected group behavior; gated and topk variants did not show the same explained-variance improvement. Normal SAE width changed the number of decoder vectors learned per circle plane.

fits_no_version.finding: In GPT-2 layer 7, reconstructions from the top 25 SAE latents on month tokens show a circle in PCA dimensions 3-4. Many latents are needed to span the month and weekday planes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Known circular (multi-dimensional) features in GPT-2 are recoverable from SAE latents, but are split across many latents.

fits_no_version.finding: On planted circles in superposition, normal SAEs at 2x width learn about 2x as many decoder vectors per circle plane.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature splitting of multi-dimensional features scales with dictionary width.

record.problems: The author says the results are almost a year old, success is hard to measure, ground truth examples are few, and the experiments do not resolve whether grouped latents are genuine multidimensional features or correlated one-dimensional features. Many reported outcomes are qualitative, without numerical values or uncertainty estimates.

untested.parts: All of it: no network learns superposition; the circles are planted by construction.
Not tested beyond reusing SAE latents on GPT-2 layer 7 as a tool.
Not tested directly. Width-dependent splitting is reported only as a method nuisance.
The post uses prior evidence of circular features. It explicitly cannot tell multi-dimensional features from correlated 1-D features.

record.verdict_notes: This is a LessWrong negative-results post evaluating a method. All results are qualitative, with no numbers or uncertainty. The reader's V1/V4/V6 labels are rejected: the rows measure SAE method performance on planted or previously known structure.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test a sparsity-dependent transition, feature importance, or whether overlap is generally nearly orthogonal.
Does not test whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure.
Tests SAE recovery of known circular subspaces in GPT-2, not whether real-model features generally spread across neurons or are sparse across a wider range of models.
Does not establish whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.

Does not establish whether the model's underlying features are inherently one-dimensional or multidimensional; the author notes ambiguity between multidimensional features and correlated one-dimensional features.

rows.subject: normal SAE
rows.operation_detail: Measured recovery of synthetic circles using decoder vectors projected into each circle plane.
rows.value: The SAE successfully finds the circles; L0 is around optimal; MSE is ~0.5 of variance recovered.
rows.note: The post says a naive solution should require 4 vectors per circle because activations cannot be negative. This does not directly measure near-orthogonality.
rows.check: This is an SAE trained on an author-constructed sum of circles, not a toy network learning superposition. It measures the SAE's recovery, not V1 geometry, and does not address whether features are 1-D.

rows.subject: normal SAE
rows.operation_detail: Measured recovery of synthetic circles using decoder vectors projected into each circle plane.
rows.value: The SAE successfully finds the circles; L0 is around optimal; MSE is ~0.5 of variance recovered.
rows.note: The post reports the same qualitative recovery and metric description for both normal SAEs.
rows.check: Same as r1: it measures the method's recovery of planted circles. It is also a near-duplicate of r1.

rows.subject: normal SAEs, width = 1600 * 8 and width = 1600 * 16
rows.operation_detail: Compared the number of learned decoder vectors per circle plane.
rows.value: The bigger SAE learned about twice as many decoder vectors per plane as the smaller SAE.
rows.note: The post describes this as clear feature splitting between the two SAEs.
rows.check: Feature splitting by SAE width on planted data is a property of the dictionary method, not of a model's representation.

rows.subject: Group SAE
rows.operation_detail: Examined the learned groups and within-group decoder vectors on synthetic circles; added a loss term for the ReLU of pairwise within-group dot products.
rows.measure: Whether groups align with circle planes and whether vectors within groups are perpendicular
rows.value: Groups learned features in the same ground-truth circle plane, but initially learned duplicate copies of the same vector. The added loss made each group's vectors perpendicular; multiple groups per plane remained.
rows.note: The author says the multiple-groups-per-plane problem was never solved.
rows.check: This records the study's own Group SAE behaviour. It is a method-performance row.

rows.subject: Group SAE
rows.operation_detail: Ablated the reconstruction to the top 25 layer 7 SAE features activated by examples ending in a month token, then examined the resulting representation and feature activation patterns.

conditions.value: sentences from the Pile ending in a month of the year token

rows.measure: Circular subspace and feature activation patterns across months
rows.value: A circle appeared in the third and fourth PCA dimensions. Many grouped SAE features fired on multiple close together months, rather than mostly on single months. Both SAE types required many features to span the weekday and month planes; about half of the 25 grouped SAE vectors came from the same group as another selected vector.
rows.locator: Do the Group SAEs Capture Known Circular Subspaces
rows.note: The post says Group SAE latents seemed less directed toward clusters of individual months than normal SAE latents.
rows.check: It compares the Group SAE with a normal SAE, i.e. the study's method against an alternative.

rows.value: Normal SAE features fired mostly on single months.
rows.locator: Do the Group SAEs Capture Known Circular Subspaces

rows.subject: Group SAE
rows.operation_detail: Compared high-level SAE metrics and within-group feature similarity with ReLU SAEs.
rows.measure: Explained variance, CE loss score, maximum intra-cosine similarities, feature duplication, and within-group Jaccard similarity
rows.baseline: ReLU SAE at the same sparsity
rows.value: Explained variance and CE loss score were a little bit higher. There was some evidence of less feature splitting from lower maximum intra-cosine similarities, but feature duplication was high. The Jaccard similarity between the two latents in many groups was very high.
rows.locator: Training Group SAEs on GPT-2 — High level metrics
rows.note: The author says the groups seemed semantically related, but does not establish that they are genuinely multidimensional features.
rows.check: It compares Group SAE and ReLU SAE metrics. This is method performance.
